chunks: And from him, from Abdul Momin, from Dawood ibn Abu Suleyman Al-Jasas, from Uzafir who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'What prevents you from performing Hajj every year?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, the dependents.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If you were to die, then who would be there for your dependents? Feed your dependants vinegar and oil, and perform Hajj with them every year.'

key_terms.فِدَاكَ: May I be your ransom/sacrifice (a term of respect)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about balancing family responsibilities with the obligation of Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prioritizes the spiritual obligation of Hajj over the material provision of dependents, illustrating a pragmatic approach to balancing religious duty with family welfare. By suggesting sustenance with simple staples like vinegar and oil, he emphasizes that the spiritual benefit of annual pilgrimage outweighs the cost of modest living, ensuring the provider remains present to care for the family rather than leaving them orphaned by death.
